dependency: Preferred dependency: existing numbered open trays plus unassisted self-service shelf return. ATT intervention hypothesis: disable self-service shelf return for the single additional twenty-minute block and require attended handback at the checkout table. Borrowers finish their full five-minute allowance before handback; no current loan is interrupted. Numbered trays remain necessary loan containers under C1, but the return operation no longer relies on an unattended open tray awaiting a shelf count. One volunteer receives each handback and watches tray and loose-counter placement while the second independently counts the selected returned tray. The intake mat remains usable, with at most one tray under inspection. This explicitly sacrifices the preferred ability to return without waiting for a volunteer; queue delay must be measured rather than hidden by restoring shelf drop-off.

predictions.account: H1: borrower-delayed completion of the corresponding return, a hypothesis rather than an observed cause.
predictions.when: During an attended handback that produces an independently confirmed initial count of eleven, the receiving volunteer records seconds and watches subsequent borrower counter placement without moving counters among loans; repeat selected counts at placement and one, three, and five minutes if attention permits.
predictions.result: H1 predicts some watched borrowers place a final counter after their tray, followed by agreement on twelve when that directly witnessed counter is included. Observing only an initially complete attended return would also fit an effect of the changed procedure and would not establish that historical loose counters belonged to their short trays. An unwatched arrival cannot establish origin.

predictions.account: H2: traffic or volunteer handling redistributes counters between loans and the shared mat, a competing hypothesis.
predictions.when: During the same block, record observed volunteer moves and borrower traffic before any selected tray shortage is filled; inspect only one return at a time and compare mat and tray counts at the fixed checkpoints.
predictions.result: H2 predicts directly observed movements unrelated to a selected borrower can change mat or tray counts, and preventing unobserved mixing may reduce apparent later recoveries. A loose counter that appears without a watched corresponding transfer remains unattributed and cannot validate delayed return. A reduction in shortages alone distinguishes neither H2 from H1 nor either from a procedural effect.

predictions.account: H3: inaccurate single-person counts, a competing hypothesis.
predictions.when: Before the block, obtain two separately recorded counts of the five proposed complete kits, then obtain separate counts of each selected return before any counter movement; record disagreements and any subsequent recount rather than selecting a count as correct by default.
predictions.result: H3 predicts some discrepancies between independently recorded counts without a witnessed counter transfer. Repeated agreement on eleven following independently checked checkout would weaken that count-error explanation for that selected loan, but would not prove actual loss or identify historical counter origins. Agreement can still share error.

surviving_outcome: Candidate surviving valued outcome: explaining short returns sufficiently to choose a bounded change while maintaining at least five complete twelve-counter kits and resolving each return within five minutes of placement. Seventy-one accounted counters permit five complete kits plus eleven remaining counters, subject to verified counts; the incomplete sixth kit cannot be issued. The attended procedure may preserve the five complete kits as serviceable loan inventory, including kits temporarily with borrowers, but cannot guarantee five simultaneously ready for checkout during active loans. Keep the eleven remaining counters accounted separately instead of assigning unattributed mat counters to a particular loan as evidence of its return. Log placement time, count disagreement, observed moves, queue length, active loans, and time remaining with the stopwatch and tally. Allocate both volunteers within forty total minutes and use only this block; late placements permit at most the remainder of the block for observation, so do not promise a full five-minute follow-up that would require a second block. If a selected shortage remains unresolved at its five-minute deadline, or observation ends earlier, record that limitation and do not claim the reconciliation criterion succeeded. This is a dependency-breaking feasibility hypothesis; the stipulated record establishes neither success nor the cause. Necessity of twelve counters per issued kit and conservation of the accounted pool constrain feasibility, but do not establish H1, H2, or H3.
unknowns: The original loose-counter origins remain unknown because historical transfers were unwatched and counters are visually indistinguishable.
Whether two volunteers can attend handbacks, independently count, and record enough transfer evidence within one twenty-minute block without excessive waiting is unknown.

Whether at least five complete kits can remain serviceable after a new genuinely unresolved shortage, with no spare counters, is unknown; the eleven remaining counters provide a bounded pool but any replenishment must be logged and cannot prove borrower return.
The unresolved counter location, independent count accuracy, and causes of the closing-time concentration remain unknown.

Eliminating self-service changes transfer behavior and handling together; differences from the old record do not uniquely identify a cause, and absence of a new anomaly in one block would leave the rival accounts unresolved.
Whether every return can be reconciled within five minutes is untested, particularly for placements near block end; unresolved events must remain unresolved rather than be called successful.
